Technology stocks advanced on Wednesday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding slightly more than 0.7% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index also was posting a more than 0.7% gain.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Hewlett Packard ( HPQ ) was over 4% higher in late Wednesday trading after the computer manufacturer reported above-consensus fiscal Q2 revenue. Revenue rose to $14.00 billion during the three months ended April 30 from $12.38 billion during the same quarter last year, topping the Capital IQ consensus expecting $13.57 billion in revenue. Excluding one-time items, H-P earned $0.48 during the quarter, up from $0.40 per share during the year-ago period and matching Street views. Looking ahead, the company is projecting non-GAAP fiscal Q3 net income in a range of $0.49 to $0.52 per share and adjusted FY19 earnings of between $1.97 to $2.02 per share. Analysts are expecting the company to earn $0.49 per share during the current quarter and $1.97 per share this year. The company Wednesday also said it has named Steve Fieler as its new chief financial officer, effective July 1. He succeeds Cathie Lesjak, who will become interim chief operating officer.
In other sector news:
+ Analog Devices ( ADI ) was still on positive ground Wednesday, backing down from a nearly 3% gain earlier in the session that followed the chipmaker reporting Q2 results topping Wall Street expectations. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $1.45 per share during the three months ended May 5, up from $1.03 during the year-ago period and surpassing the Capital IQ consensus by $0.18 per share. Revenue increased to $1.51 billion from $1.21 billion last year, also exceeding the $1.47 billion Street view. The company is projecting Q3 net income in a range of $1.38 to $1.52 per share on between $1.47 billion to $1.55 billion in revenue. Analysts, on average, are projecting Q3 of $1.40 on $1.49 billion in revenue.
- Evine Live ( EVLV ) was little changed Wednesday afternoon, swinging between moderate gains and losses, after reporting a wider-than-expected Q1 net loss. The digital commerce company generated a net loss of $0.05 per share during the three months ended May 5, unchanged from the same quarter last year compared with the Capital IQ consensus expecting a $0.02 per share net loss. Total revenue rose to $156.5 million from $156.3 million during the year-ago period and roughly matching the $156 million Street view.
